subject: Request: customer-managed infra SLA attenuation / latency carve-out (Cerulean Systems)
messages:
From: Alan King <alan.king@ceruleansys.com>
To: diego_fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-15T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request for carve-out language for customer-managed network incidents

Diego —

Thanks for taking this. We’re in the middle of onboarding Redwood Private into our primary colocation (Equator DC) and have a few constraints on our side that make some of the standard uptime/latency commitments difficult to meet in practice. Specifically:

- A portion of our traffic traverses a customer-managed WAN (third-party MPLS/SD-WAN) where we currently see periodic maintenance windows and occasional latency spikes (100–250 ms) tied to upstream providers.
- We control the datacenter edge (BGP and firewall policies) and perform scheduled changes on our cadence (not aligned with Redwood maintenance windows).

Can Redwood provide a short contract appendix that:
1) Excludes incidents caused solely by customer-controlled network elements from Redwood’s uptime/latency SLA;
2) Defines how latency SLOs are measured (ingress at app/API endpoint vs. edge-to-edge) and whether we can exclude path segments outside Redwood’s control; and
3) Includes a mutual action process for incident verification (we can produce network incident timelines).

I’ve attached a rough network topology and an extract of recent incident windows for context (Cerulean-Network-Topology.pdf). Would appreciate a proposed appendix or redline we can review.

—Alan
Alan King
Director of Infrastructure, Cerulean Systems
alan.king@ceruleansys.com
From: diego_fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Alan King <alan.king@ceruleansys.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-15T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request for carve-out language for customer-managed network incidents

Alan —

Appreciate the context and the topology — that helps. I’m looping in Marissa (Customer Success) and Marcus (Legal) so we can cover operational and contractual angles. High level response: we commonly support narrow carve-outs for customer-controlled infrastructure, but the language needs to be precise about measurement points and evidence required.

Next steps I propose:
- Marcus to draft a short SLA appendix with clear definitions ("Customer-Controlled Network Incident"), measurement point (Redwood ingress), and evidence requirements.
- Marissa to propose an observational trial (30 days) where both sides run passive monitoring to align baselines.
- We’ll request detailed incident logs from Cerulean when a claim is made (timestamps, traceroutes, provider outage tickets).

I’ve attached a quick questionnaire we use for private deployments to capture topology and monitoring configuration (redwood_questionnaire_private_deploy.pdf). Can you fill that and send back? Also, would you be available for a brief sync tomorrow (30 min) to walk through the topology and expected exclusions?

Best,
Diego
Diego Fernandez
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
DiegoFernandez@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0184
From: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: diego_fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>, Alan King <alan.king@ceruleansys.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-16T09:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request for carve-out language for customer-managed network incidents

Alan / Diego / Marissa —

Thanks for the context. Attached is a first-pass SLA appendix (redwood_sla_appendix_v1.docx) that attempts to be narrow and objective. Key points:

1) Definition: "Customer-Controlled Network Incident" — an incident where the root cause, supported by traceroute/BGP announcements or third-party outage notices, is attributable to network elements fully operated by the Customer or Customer-selected transit providers.

2) Measurement point: throughput/latency SLOs are measured at the Redwood ingress (the IP/hostname we expose to the customer endpoint). Any latency or packet loss observed only on path segments upstream of that ingress IP is considered outside Redwood’s operational control and excluded from availability calculations.

3) Evidence & verification: Customer must provide incident timeline + supporting artifacts (traceroutes, provider incident ticket numbers, configuration change logs) within 72 hours of claiming an exclusion. Redwood will validate with passive monitoring and, if necessary, a mutual third-party packet-capture for the event window.

4) Scope & limits: Exclusions are limited to network incidents and do not apply to failures of Redwood-managed components (serving runtime, storage, or control plane). Additionally, repeated systemic failures on the customer-controlled path (more than 3 incidents in a rolling 90-day window) will trigger a review and potential scheduling of joint remediation work.

Please review and call out any items you can’t accept. From a legal standpoint we want to avoid black-box exclusions — the appendix aims to be verifiable and time-boxed.

—Marcus Lin
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.ai
From: Alan King <alan.king@ceruleansys.com>
To: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, diego_fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-16T15:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request for carve-out language for customer-managed network incidents

Marcus / Team —

Thanks, that draft is reasonable and close to what we had in mind. A couple of clarifications from Cerulean’s side:

- Measurement point: we prefer SLO measurement at our application ingress (so both sides agree on a single public IP/hostname). We can create a monitoring feed (Grafana / Prometheus endpoints) for the 30-day trial so both teams see the same telemetry.
- Latency SLOs: Cerulean is proposing 95th percentile < 100 ms for internal-app calls (post-ingress) but is willing to accept exclusions where the customer WAN shows > 30% packet loss or confirmed provider outage.
- Evidence: we can provide traceroutes, provider ticket numbers and a CSV export of our edge firewall logs for any claimed event (attached: cerulean_network_incident_log.csv).

If you’re okay, can we:
1)  Lock the appendix language with one small edit to the measurement-point clause (specify the agreed host/IP);
2)  Kick off the 30-day observational window starting Monday 2027-09-20; and
3)  Use DocuSign to finalize the appendix if the trial matches expectations.

I’m attaching our incident extract for the past 60 days for your review (cerulean_network_incident_log.csv).

—Alan
Alan King
Director of Infrastructure, Cerulean Systems
alan.king@ceruleansys.com
From: diego_fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Alan King <alan.king@ceruleansys.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-17T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request for carve-out language for customer-managed network incidents

Alan —

This all sounds workable. We’ll make the measurement-point explicit (the public host you nominate) and incorporate the 30-day observation window starting 2027-09-20. Action items below:

- Marcus: will update the appendix with the single-host measurement clause and a tightened evidence deadline (72 hours), then circulate for e-signature.
- Marissa: will coordinate the monitoring config and provide the Grafana dashboard template + runbook for incident callbacks.
- Alan/Cerulean: please confirm the public host/IP you want Redwood to use as the official ingress measurement point and upload the completed questionnaire.

If we all agree, I’ll ask Legal to issue the DocuSign envelope and Marissa will schedule the kickoff call. Thanks for the quick turnaround on the logs — they were helpful.

Best,
Diego
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
DiegoFernandez@redwood.ai
